question.text: Bank Rate differs from Repo Rate in that:

answer.text: Bank Rate is always lower than Repo Rate
Bank Rate is for medium to long term or emergency lending without collateral, while Repo Rate is for short-term lending against securities
Bank Rate is set by SEBI while Repo Rate is set by RBI
There is no difference between them

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 97 of the NISM Series XV workbook, the Repo Rate applies when the central bank lends to commercial banks against approved securities for a very short term. Bank Rate is the rate at which RBI lends to commercial banks without any collateral for medium-to-long term or emergency needs. The Trap: Both rates are set by RBI (the central bank and monetary authority), not SEBI. The distinguishing features per the source are the collateral requirement and tenor, not the relative level of the two rates. Note: Source-backed distinction is collateral (securities for repo, none for bank rate) and tenor (very short term for repo, medium-to-long term/emergency for bank rate).
